Commentary.Commentary: Right then! That's it for today's coverage of the match between Zimbabwe and Ireland. The series has walked us to a dead end but there are so many matches going around in the world. The ICC Champions Trophy 2025 is a big clash between Afghanistan and England. That match is scheduled to be played on 26th February, Tuesday at 9 am GMT. But as you know, you can always join us early for all the build-up to the action. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

Sikandar Raza strides forward to accept the trophy from the Director of the Zimbabwe Cricket Board, a testament to their hard-fought success. With a contagious sense of excitement, he beckons his teammates to join him. As they gather around the trophy, their faces light up with pride and joy, perfectly embodying the spirit of teamwork and dedication that brought them this victory. This moment is not just a snapshot; it's a celebration of their incredible journey and a reminder of what can be achieved through perseverance and unity.

Sikandar Raza, the skipper of Zimbabwe started off praising the relentless performance of Tony Munyonga. Also says that Trevor Gwandu has set the bar high for the team. Continues that they were able to put a good total on board. Reckons that they have worked really hard in the last 6-7 months which is showing it's color. Ends up saying that every time their chips are down some or other players always stand up and delivery, which is really important for the moral of the team.

Paul Stirling, the skipper of Ireland reckons that it would have been a really good game. He believes that they were on top at times but unfortunately, the weather was in a different mood. Also says that Craig Young was brilliant and has done exceptionally well. Ends up saying that he and his team had a lovely time in Zimbabwe and they will surely roam around this beautiful country.
Presentation Time...

In their 18-over match against Ireland, which was hampered by weather, Zimbabwe had set a lofty goal of 142 runs. Sikandar Raza, the skipper, gave vital stability following a difficult start with early wickets, setting the stage for a potent middle-order performance. They achieved a competitive total thanks to their aggressive batting in the last overs. The bowling squad is now prepared to show off their abilities and stave off Ireland's pursuit. Zimbabwe is ready to win!

UPDATE - 7.56 pm GMT - It has happened—exactly what we were desperately hoping to avoid. The match has been ABANDONED DUE TO RAIN, which means, Zimbabwe won the Twenty 20 series against Ireland. It’s a tough blow for the Men in Greens and their passionate supporters, but this is the nature of cricket. Let's take this moment to rally behind our team and look ahead to future matches, determined for a brighter outcome!

UPDATE - 7.29 pm GMT - A few officials with the umbrella have walked their way to the center of the pitch. They are having a long discussion. The rain may be relentless, yet it's holding steady, not picking up pace. As we near the crucial cut-off time of 8:04 pm GMT for a thrilling 5-over chase, let’s remain hopeful that the skies will clear. Together, let’s keep our fingers crossed for an exhilarating display of cricket!

UPDATE - 7.10 pm GMT - Oh no! Once again, the rain gods are threatening to drench our excitement. The covers are swiftly being deployed to shield the track from the downpour. The ground staff is laboring tirelessly, maneuvering massive sheets to protect the field. Yet, amidst the uncertainty, let's hold onto hope and stay optimistic about witnessing the thrilling continuation of this captivating encounter!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

For Ireland, Gareth Delany and Craig Young stood out with their remarkable performance, taking two wickets in just one over. Meanwhile, Matthew Humphreys and Joshua Little each contributed by claiming one wicket, helping to keep Zimbabwe in check. With a competitive total now on the board, Zimbabwe will be eager to apply pressure on the Irish batters as they embark on their chase. The stage is set for an exhilarating contest, so stay tuned for all the action!

Brain Bennett's swift exit left Zimbabwe in a precarious position at 67/4, but the duo of Tony Munyonga and Tashinga Musekiwa stepped up with a crucial partnership of 39 runs off 22 balls. Their valuable contributions revitalized the innings and allowed the team to finish strong. This late-order surge was instrumental in propelling Zimbabwe to a respectable total, especially considering the challenging conditions. Their heroic effort not only steadied the ship but also set a competitive benchmark for the opposing team to chase.

Zimbabwe has set a formidable target of 142 runs in their rain-affected 18-over showdown against Ireland. The match started on a shaky note, with wickets falling at regular intervals, but it was the captain, Sikandar Raza, who stepped up to provide much-needed stability. His inning was a testament to resilience, and even though he fell victim in the 10th over, he laid a solid foundation that the middle order capitalized on with vigor. In a thrilling finish, their aggressive batting in the closing overs propelled Zimbabwe to a competitive total. Now all eyes are on their bowling unit, poised to unleash their skills and thwart Ireland's pursuit. With determination and strategy, Zimbabwe is ready to defend its total and seize victory!

OUT! PEACH OF A DELIVERY! Matthew Humphreys joins the party now! Short, and outside off, around the seventh stump, turns it in sharply towards the stump. Wessly Madhevere hangs back and tries to cut but gets beaten on the inner edge. The ball zips in so fast that Madhevere can't react quickly.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Craig Young got four scalps in the previous encounter against the Chevrons and yet again he continues with his masterclass! Young bowls it on a length, on off, nips it away from the left-hander. Tadiwanashe Marumani tries to pat it towards his off side but catches the outer edge. The ball zips towards left of the keeper and Lorcan Tucker makes no mistake to glove that one.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Matthew Humphreys to Tadiwanashe Marumani, 5 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: All set to start the match! Due to the late start of the match, it will be an 18-over contest and the first five overs will be the powerplay over. The umpires have stepped on the green turf, followed by the players of Ireland. Tadiwanashe Marumani will face the first delivery for Zimbabwe, and Brian Bennett will be partnering up with him. Matthew Humphreys will get the job to bowl the first over for the Men in Greens. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Victor Empitsang is pitchside. He says It is still a good surface. There's some grass covering. Greener and moisture on the surface. The bowlers will get some early advantage. Batters have to stay there and bat deep to get some advantage.

Sikandar Raza, the skipper of Zimbabwe says that they would like to bowl first as well because of the rain but his side is also confident with the bat first. Also says that there will be a little bit of moisture on the tracks. Ends up saying there are a lot of ups and downs in the series but they will make sure to finish at the top.

Paul Stirling, the skipper of Ireland says that it's an easy task to bat second under the lights as they are not certainly sure about the conditions. Continues that they had a good time in Zimbabwe playing the series. Ends up saying that they have three changes and they are going to see some new faces perform for the badge.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Tim Tector, Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Gareth Delany, Fionn Hand, Matthew Humphreys, Craig Young, Josh Little

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Brian Bennett, Tadiwanashe Marumani (WK), Wessly Madhevere, Sikandar Raza (C), Tony Munyonga, Ryan Burl, Tashinga Musekiwa, Wellington Masakadza, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani, Trevor Gwandu
TOSS! Paul Stirling, the skipper of Ireland won the toss and decided to BOWL first.
UPDATE - 4.53 pm GMT - Our wishes have come alive! We are ready for the toss as the two captains are ready with the coin at the centre of the pitch.
UPDATE - 4.24 pm GMT - BETTER SIGHTS! The rains have stopped and the ground staffs are working hard to soak the logged water out of the ground. The umpires will have an inspection at 5.00 pm GMT.

UPDATE - 4.09 pm GMT - Just the news we were afraid of! We are currently experiencing a minor setback in the toss due to light rain at Harare Sports Club. The good news is that the weather is expected to clear up shortly. We’ll keep you informed with live updates the moment the toss is underway. Stay with us for all the excitement!

The weather in Harare may be a bit concerning, with light rain potentially looming overhead. However, let’s remain hopeful and passionately optimistic for an exhilarating and seamless cricket match! Let’s rally behind the teams, the players, and all the dedicated fans who are eagerly anticipating some thrilling action on the field. Together, we can turn any challenge into an unforgettable experience!

On the other hand, Zimbabwe holds all the momentum and is just one win away from claiming the series for themselves. Their middle order is formidable, with players like Sikandar Raza, Ryan Burl, and Tony Munyonga capable of anchoring the innings at any stage. The bowling unit has been remarkably economical, providing them with a distinct advantage in taking wickets. The Chevrons will aim to replicate this impressive performance in today’s match as they strive for glory.

Ireland has struggled to find the spark needed to overcome the Chevrons. In their recent outing, only Lorcan Tucker, Harry Tector, and Curtis Campher managed to step up with double-digit scores, highlighting the overall performance of the team. On the bowling front, Craig Young showcased remarkable skill by taking four wickets and dismantling the top order, but the team failed to capitalize on that early advantage. The bowlers need to sharpen their line and length, as too many boundaries were conceded in the last match. Paul Stirling and the rest of the squad are determined to regroup and come back stronger as a cohesive unit.

Greetings to all the passionate cricket fans joining us for the thrilling finale of this three-match Twenty20 series! Today, Ireland steps onto the pitch to challenge Zimbabwe at the iconic Harare Sports Club. With Zimbabwe currently at the helm of the series, the stakes couldn't be higher for Ireland. This is their final opportunity to seize the moment and flip the script! Don’t miss out on this exciting showdown as anything can happen in the world of cricket!
... MATCHDAY ...

The third and final T20I between Zimbabwe and Ireland is set to take place, with the hosts looking to seal the series after their win in the second match. The first game was unfortunately washed out, but Zimbabwe made the most of the opportunity in the second match, edging past the visitors. In the previous game, Ireland's Lorcan Tucker, Harry Tector, and Curtis Campher showed promise with the bat. Still, the rest of the lineup failed to capitalize, resulting in a below-par total. Zimbabwe's top order also struggled, but their middle order, led by a brilliant knock from Tony Munyonga, stepped up to guide the team to victory. As the series comes to a close, Ireland will be looking to bounce back and level the series, while Zimbabwe will aim to wrap up the series with a win. The match promises to be an exciting contest, with both teams eager to make a statement. Can Ireland's batting lineup fire on all cylinders, or will Zimbabwe's middle order continue to prove decisive? The stage is set for a thrilling finale.
